main_investors: Concept Ventures, Redpoint Ventures, SV Angel, Torch Capital, Anamacara
description:
Anam was founded in London in 2024 by Caoimhe Murphy and Ben Carr, who had previously worked together at the AI video company Synthesia. The company raised a GBP 1.75 million pre-seed round led by Concept Ventures, followed by a USD 9 million seed round in 2025 with participation from SV Angel, Torch Capital, Concept Ventures and angel investors, bringing reported total funding to roughly USD 11.3 million.
Anam builds real-time, photorealistic AI personas, sometimes described as digital humans, that give conversational AI a human face. The product combines low-latency streaming infrastructure with APIs so that product teams can add a visual persona to voice or text assistants, targeting use cases such as customer support, sales, training and education.
The company sells its technology as a developer-facing platform and API for businesses that embed AI personas into their own products and customer interactions.
confidence_notes: Année de fondation: Vestbee et Forbes indiquent 2024; un agrégateur secondaire (AI Market Watch) indique 2023 — 2024 retenu (sources plus fiables). Montant total (11,3 M$) provient d'agrégateurs (Tracxn/AI Market Watch), pas d'un communiqué officiel. Effectif non confirmé (fourchette 11-50 selon agrégateur). Modèle économique décrit de façon générique faute de page tarifaire consultée.

main_investors: Bessemer Venture Partners, Decibel Partners, Bain Future Back Ventures, MVP Ventures, 645 Ventures
description:
Strella was founded in 2023 by Lydia Hylton and Priya Krishnan, who met in high school. Their first version of the product was a manual 'Wizard of Oz' prototype in which a co-founder simulated an AI moderator on video calls before the underlying models were built. In October 2025 the company announced a USD 14 million Series A led by Bessemer Venture Partners with participation from Decibel Partners, Bain Future Back Ventures, MVP Ventures and 645 Ventures.
Strella offers an AI-powered customer research platform. An AI moderator conducts in-depth interviews, adapting in real time to participant answers and probing further like a human researcher, while the platform automates recruiting, scheduling and real-time synthesis. The company says this lets teams run hundreds of interviews in hours rather than weeks.
Strella sells the platform to enterprise research, product and marketing teams; publicly reported users include Amazon, Chobani and Duolingo.
confidence_notes: Siège: New York déduit de la couverture Built In NYC et du profil LinkedIn de l'entreprise; non confirmé par une page 'contact' officielle consultée. Total levé 18 M$ issu de Tracxn (14 M$ Série A confirmés par communiqué). Effectif non trouvé.

main_investors: Index Ventures, Blackstone Innovations Investments, Greylock, CRV
description:
7AI was founded in 2024 by Lior Div and Yonatan Striem-Amit, co-founders of the endpoint security company Cybereason, and came out of stealth in February 2025. In December 2025 it announced a USD 130 million Series A led by Index Ventures with participation from new investor Blackstone Innovations Investments, described by the company as the largest Series A in cybersecurity history and valuing it at about USD 700 million; total funding stands at USD 166 million.
7AI builds an agentic security platform that takes on the non-human work of the security operations center. Swarms of AI agents detect, investigate, respond to and hunt threats end to end, with human analysts kept 'on the loop' rather than in it; the company reports having processed more than 9 million alerts in production and cutting false positives by 95-99 percent.
The company sells to enterprise security teams and states that it scales through a channel-first go-to-market model.
confidence_notes: Greylock et CRV proviennent d'un agrégateur (AI Market Watch) pour le tour d'amorçage, non confirmés par communiqué; Index Ventures et Blackstone sont confirmés. Effectif: un agrégateur annonce ~110, non vérifié, donc null. Valorisation 700 M$ mentionnée par CRN, non intégrée aux champs structurés.

main_investors: Mayfield Fund, Menlo Ventures, Celesta Capital
founders: Rajiv Khemani, Liang Li, Jean-Luc Coelho, Viswesh Ananthakrishnan, Patrick Xu
description:
Aurascape was incorporated in California in May 2024 and operated in stealth for about a year before launching publicly in April 2025 with USD 50 million in funding. The round was led by Mayfield Fund and Menlo Ventures, with strategic participation from Celesta Capital and individual investors including former Palo Alto Networks CEO Mark McLaughlin, former Symantec CEO Greg Clark and Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan.
Aurascape builds an AI-native security platform that secures how enterprises use AI. It provides real-time visibility into AI application usage, intent-based controls, protection of sensitive data and automated governance, addressing the 'shadow AI' problem created when employees adopt AI tools outside of IT oversight.
The company sells its platform to enterprise security and IT organisations.
confidence_notes: Montant total incohérent selon les sources: 50 M$ annoncés en avril 2025 (communiqué), 62,8 M$ selon Tracxn (2026), 39 M$ selon FundedIQ. Valeur la plus récente et la plus élevée (62,8) retenue par pondération récence x fiabilité — à vérifier. Effectif 64 issu de PitchBook (snippet). Le prénom complet du fondateur 'Rajiv K' (Tracxn) a été complété en Rajiv Khemani via le registre californien et un profil fondateur.

main_investors: Accel, Meritech, Alt Capital, BoxGroup, Liquid 2 Ventures, Mantis VC, SV Angel
description:
depthfirst is an applied AI lab founded in October 2024 in San Francisco by technical leaders previously at Google DeepMind, Databricks, Faire and Amazon. Co-founder Daniele Perito was a co-founder of Faire and previously director of security and risk engineering at Square, while co-founder Andrea Michi was a research engineering lead at Google DeepMind. In January 2026 the company announced a USD 40 million Series A led by Accel, followed by an USD 80 million Series B; Forbes reported a valuation of about USD 580 million in March 2026.
The company develops what it calls General Security Intelligence: custom AI agents and security models that work continuously to identify, triage and remediate vulnerabilities across software and infrastructure layers, positioned as a defence against AI-driven exploitation.
depthfirst sells to enterprises and reported customers include ClickUp, Lovable, Supabase, incident.io, AngelList and Moveworks.
confidence_notes: Total levé estimé à 120 M$ = 40 M$ (Série A) + 80 M$ (Série B); un éventuel amorçage antérieur n'est pas comptabilisé. Un troisième cofondateur au nom de famille 'Mithani' (ex-Databricks/AWS) est mentionné par Dealroom mais son prénom n'a pas été confirmé, il n'est donc pas listé. Effectif non trouvé.

main_investors: Wing Venture Capital, Norwest Venture Partners, S Capital
description:
Lumana was founded in 2021 by Sagi Ben Moshe, previously chief incubation officer and general manager of the Emerging Growth and Incubation Group at Intel, following Intel's acquisition of his 3D imaging company. The company emerged from stealth and, in 2025, closed a USD 40 million Series A led by Wing Venture Capital with support from existing investors Norwest and S Capital, bringing total funding to about USD 64 million.
Lumana sells an AI video intelligence platform that uses vision language models and agentic AI to turn existing security cameras into intelligent sensors, enabling real-time monitoring, automated event detection, alerting and faster incident response with near-human-like perception.
The company delivers a hybrid-cloud offering combining hardware, cloud software and AI analytics for enterprise customers; it reported surpassing 50,000 connected cameras.
confidence_notes: Siège: Palo Alto selon PrivCo et VCBacked; une autre source (Startup Intros) indique Los Gatos avec un centre R&D à Tel Aviv — divergence non tranchée. D'éventuels cofondateurs autres que Sagi Ben Moshe n'ont pas été confirmés. Effectif non trouvé.

description:
Prophet Security was co-founded by Kamal Shah, who serves as CEO, and Vibhav Sreekanti, who serves as CTO. The company launched publicly with an agentic AI SOC analyst product and has since raised multiple rounds, including a USD 30 million round reported by VentureBeat; aggregators place total funding at about USD 41 million across three rounds from investors including Accel and Bain Capital Ventures.
The company builds an Agentic AI SOC Platform that automates the triage, investigation and remediation of security alerts. Its AI agents synthesise incoming alerts, correlate data across sources and produce investigations; the product line has expanded to include an AI Detection Engineer that finds detection gaps, builds and tunes detection rules and maintains a live MITRE ATT&CK coverage map, as well as an AI Threat Hunter.
Prophet Security sells its platform to enterprise security operations teams and reports SOC 2 Type 2 compliance.
confidence_notes: Ville de siège et année de fondation non confirmées par les pages consultées (la page About Us de l'entreprise ne les mentionne pas) — laissées à null. Total levé (41 M$) provient de Tracxn, snippet uniquement; le tour de 30 M$ est confirmé par VentureBeat. Effectif non trouvé.

main_investors: Icon Ventures, Firebolt Ventures, Cota Capital, Wipro Ventures
description:
Simbian was founded in 2023 by Ambuj Kumar and emerged from stealth in April 2024 with a USD 10 million round from investors including Icon Ventures, Firebolt Ventures, Cota Capital and Wipro, with the stated goal of building a fully autonomous security platform.
The company builds an AI security operations platform staffed by autonomous agents. Its SOC agent triages alerts coming from SIEM and XDR tools by applying institutional knowledge and organisational playbooks, and the platform extends to threat hunting, penetration testing and GRC workflows around a unified context layer the company calls the Simbian Context Lake.
Simbian sells to enterprises and managed security service providers, integrating with their existing security tooling.
confidence_notes: Tracxn liste 'Ambuj Kumar et Ambuj Kumar' comme fondateurs (doublon manifeste); un éventuel second cofondateur n'a pas été identifié. Siège Mountain View issu d'une source secondaire (yespress). Montant total 10 M$ = dernier tour connu (avril 2024); des tours plus récents pourraient exister. Effectif non trouvé.

main_investors: Peak XV Partners, Y Combinator, Uncorrelated Ventures
description:
Alex was founded in 2023 by Aaron Wang and John Rytel and went through Y Combinator's Winter 2024 batch. In late 2025 the company announced a USD 17 million Series A led by Peak XV Partners with participation from Y Combinator and Uncorrelated Ventures, bringing total funding to USD 20 million.
Alex provides a voice AI recruiter that autonomously conducts initial job interviews. The platform handles phone screens, video interviews, scheduling, note-taking and fraud detection, allowing recruiting teams to interview every applicant rather than only the most obvious candidates and to shorten hiring cycles.
The company sells the product to corporate talent acquisition teams; it says it has been used by hundreds of companies, including Fortune 100 firms and large banks, and that its AI runs thousands of interviews per day.
confidence_notes: Homonymie levée: il s'agit bien d'Alex, recruteur IA vocal (domaine alex.com, YC W24). Effectif 30 issu de la fiche Y Combinator (snippet). Total 20 M$ = 17 M$ Série A + amorçage antérieur, cohérent entre plusieurs sources.

description:
Tako is a Brazilian HR and payroll company founded by Fernando Gadotti, previously a founder of DogHero. It emerged from stealth in November 2024 with a seed round of about BRL 75 million led by Andreessen Horowitz and Ribbit Capital, with participation from ONEVC and the founders of Ramp, and raised a further USD 18 million round co-led by Ribbit Capital and Andreessen Horowitz in 2025; aggregators place total funding at about USD 31.2 million.
Tako centralises payroll, onboarding, offboarding, employee data and labour compliance for mid-sized Brazilian companies. Specialised AI agents trained on Brazil's complex labour laws autonomously handle routine payroll runs, compliance checks and risk identification, escalating complex decisions to human operators.
The company sells a software platform to mid-sized companies in Brazil, organised around two products built on the same infrastructure: Payroll & People Ops and Recruiter.
confidence_notes: Homonymie levée: il s'agit de Tako, plateforme RH/paie brésilienne (et non de la startup Tako de visualisation de données). La page About mentionne au moins un second cofondateur (prénom Sebastian) non confirmé, donc non listé. Siège São Paulo déduit du profil LinkedIn du fondateur. Année de fondation 2024 = sortie de stealth; la constitution pourrait être antérieure. Une source (Dealroom) attribue le tour de R$75M à Igah Ventures, contredisant TechCrunch (a16z/Ribbit) — TechCrunch retenu.

main_investors: NEA, Threshold Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, Amex Ventures, TIAA Ventures, Crane Venture Partners, Bloomberg Beta, Laconia
founders: Alex Sherman, Andrei Dunca, Jing Feng
description:
Bluefish was founded in New York in 2024 by Alex Sherman, Andrei Dunca and Jing Feng. Sherman previously led PromoteIQ, which was acquired by Microsoft. The company raised a USD 20 million Series A led by NEA with participation from Salesforce Ventures, Crane Venture Partners, Swift Ventures and Bloomberg Beta, then a USD 43 million Series B co-led by Threshold Ventures and NEA with participation from Amex Ventures, TIAA Ventures and Salesforce Ventures, bringing total funding to USD 68 million. It has also leased its first permanent headquarters at 315 Park Avenue South in Manhattan.
Bluefish is an AI marketing platform that gives large brands visibility into and control over how AI systems such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Amazon's Rufus understand, represent and recommend them. It analyses prompt responses, measures brand performance across AI channels and enables targeted optimisation, along with brand safety management and agentic marketing capabilities.
The company sells an enterprise SaaS platform aimed at Fortune 500 brands; publicly reported customers include American Express, Hearst and Ulta Beauty.
confidence_notes: Homonymie levée: Bluefish AI (bluefishai.com), plateforme de visibilité de marque dans les assistants IA. Effectif non confirmé (fourchette 11-50 selon un agrégateur, probablement obsolète). Un agrégateur indique 24 M$ de total, chiffre antérieur à la Série B; 68 M$ retenu (Adweek + PR Newswire).

main_investors: WndrCo, Kindred Ventures, NFDG (Nat Friedman & Daniel Gross), Millennium New Horizons, Creator Ventures, Leadout Capital, Hat-Trick Capital, The MBA Fund
founders: Yinan Na, Ledell Wu, Xin Zhou
description:
Creatify was founded by Yinan Na, Ledell Wu and Xin Zhou, who had previously worked together at companies including Meta and Snap; Ledell Wu was an AI researcher at Facebook AI Research and worked on PyTorch-BigGraph and StarSpace. The company announced a USD 15.5 million Series A co-led by WndrCo, the venture fund associated with DreamWorks co-founder Jeffrey Katzenberg, and Kindred Ventures, bringing total funding to USD 23 million with earlier backing from Nat Friedman and Daniel Gross, Millennium New Horizons, Creator Ventures, Leadout Capital, Hat-Trick Capital and The MBA Fund.
Creatify is an AI platform for generating video advertising. Users paste a product link or upload visuals and descriptions and the platform produces short video ads using a library of AI avatars; its AdMax product lets marketers instantly generate, test and optimise dozens of video ads tailored for social platforms such as TikTok and Instagram.
The company sells a self-serve and business-facing SaaS product primarily to ecommerce brands and digital advertisers.
confidence_notes: Année de fondation: Tracxn indique 2022, tandis que le registre californien enregistre Creatify Lab Inc. en 2023 — 2022 retenu (fondation possiblement antérieure à l'immatriculation), à vérifier. Effectif non trouvé. Un ARR d'environ 9 M$ est cité par une source secondaire (yespress), non retenu.

description:
Newton Research was co-founded by John Hoctor, a veteran of the advertising analytics industry who previously co-founded Data Plus Math, acquired by LiveRamp, and IntegralReach, acquired by TiVo, and who holds SB and SM degrees from MIT. The company announced a USD 9 million Series A led by Greycroft and Bessemer Venture Partners, bringing total funding to just over USD 14 million raised since 2023.
Newton Research builds multi-agent AI systems for marketing analytics. Its agents automate reporting, insight generation and campaign optimisation, and let users run customer 360 analysis, build advanced models and automate analytics workflows from planning and activation through measurement, without moving the underlying data.
The company sells its platform to brands, media agencies, publishers and advertising platforms.
confidence_notes: Ville de siège non confirmée: le fondateur est basé au Massachusetts (LinkedIn) et un agrégateur cite une adresse commençant par '11100', insuffisant pour trancher — laissée à null. Année 2023 déduite de la formulation 'plus de 14 M$ levés depuis 2023' (Dealroom), non confirmée comme date de constitution. Les cofondateurs autres que John Hoctor n'ont pas été identifiés. Effectif non trouvé.

main_investors: Khosla Ventures, Saga Ventures, South Park Commons
description:
Profound was founded in 2024 by James Cadwallader and Dylan Babbs following their participation in the South Park Commons incubator. The company launched publicly in August 2024 with a USD 3.5 million seed round from investors including Khosla Ventures, Saga and South Park Commons, then raised a USD 20 million Series A to pioneer what it calls Answer Engine Optimization, and in February 2026 announced a USD 96 million Series C at a USD 1 billion valuation.
Profound helps brands understand and optimise how they appear in AI-powered search and answer engines such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews. The platform tracks brand visibility in AI-generated responses, benchmarks it through the Profound Index, and enables optimisation so that brands remain discoverable in a zero-click environment.
The company sells an enterprise SaaS platform and has been expanding into adjacent services announced with its Series C, including training, certification, an agency marketplace and Profound University.
confidence_notes: Total levé 155 M$ issu d'un agrégateur (AI Market Watch); les tours confirmés par sources primaires sont 3,5 M$ + 20 M$ + 96 M$ = 119,5 M$, un tour intermédiaire (Série B) n'ayant pas été retrouvé. Investisseurs des Séries A/B/C non confirmés (seuls les investisseurs d'amorçage le sont). Siège New York (avec bureaux à San Francisco, Londres, Buenos Aires selon un agrégateur). Effectif non retenu: estimations divergentes (100+ vs 200).
